t.7.14.1: Then he, together with his six ministers, ever fierce in strength, namely Mahodara and Prahasta, and Mārīca, Śuka and Sāraṇa,
t.7.14.2: Surrounded also by the heroic Dhūmrākṣa, ever eager for battle, the glorious one set forth, as if burning up the worlds with his wrath.
t.7.14.3: Passing in a mere moment over cities, rivers, mountains, forests and groves, he entered upon Mount Kailāsa.
t.7.14.4: But having learned that the lord of the Rākṣasas had encamped on that mountain, they said, "This is the king's brother," and went to where the Lord of Wealth was.
t.7.14.5: Having gone to him, they told him everything about his brother's resolve, and then, with Dhanada's permission, they set out for battle.
t.7.14.6: Then there arose a great commotion in the army of the lord of the Nairṛtas, like that of a swelling ocean, as if shaking the very mountain.
t.7.14.7: Then a battle arose, crowded with Yakṣas and Rākṣasas, and there the ministers of that Rākṣasa became distressed.
t.7.14.8: Seeing him and such an army, the night-roamer Daśagrīva roared with delight and then charged forward in fury.
t.7.14.10: Then Daśagrīva, though being struck with maces, iron clubs, swords, spears and lances, plunged deep into that army.
t.7.14.9: But those ministers of the lord of the Rākṣasas, men of terrible valor, each one engaged a thousand thousands in battle.
t.7.14.11: Being struck there by them as if he could not breathe, Daśānana was hemmed in by the lords of the Yakṣas, as though by clouds pouring down rain.
t.7.14.12: Then that evil-souled one, raising aloft a mace like the staff of Kāla, entered the army, sending the Yakṣas to the abode of Yama.
t.7.14.14: But in that battle, those Yakṣas were reduced to a scant remnant by his ministers, Mahodara, Śuka and the others, as clouds are scattered by the winds.
t.7.14.13: Like a fire fanned by the wind burning a vast thicket crowded with dry fuel, he burned up that most fearsome army.
t.7.14.15: Some, their limbs shattered by weapons, fell upon the field of battle; struck down to the earth, they bit their lips with their own sharp teeth.
t.7.14.16: Then, embracing one another out of fear, their weapons fallen from their hands on the battlefield, those Yakṣas sank down like riverbanks battered by the water.
t.7.14.17: What with the slain who had gone to heaven, those still fighting on the surface of the earth, and the hosts of seers looking on, no empty space remained in the sky.
t.7.14.18: Meanwhile, O Rāma, a very mighty Yakṣa named Saṃyodhakaṇṭaka arrived, with a vast army and many mounts.
t.7.14.19: Struck down by that Yakṣa as if by Viṣṇu, Mārīca fell and came to the earth, like one whose merit is exhausted falling from the sky.
t.7.14.20: Regaining consciousness after a moment and having rested, the night-wanderer fought that Yakṣa, and he, broken, fled away.
t.7.14.21: Then he entered that gateway, its parts adorned with gold and inlaid with beryl and silver, the boundary kept by the gatekeepers.
t.7.14.22: Then, O Rāma, as Daśagrīva, the night-roamer, was entering, the gatekeeper known as Sūryabhānu held him back.
t.7.14.23: Then that Yakṣa uprooted a gateway and struck the Rākṣasa with it. Yet though battered by the gateway hurled by the Yakṣa, the Rākṣasa did not fall to the ground, O Rāma, because of the boon of the Water-born One.
t.7.14.24: But he struck that Yakṣa with that very archway. The Yakṣa was then seen no more, for he had been reduced to ashes by him.
t.7.14.25: Then, seeing his prowess, all the Yakṣas fled; and, tormented by fear, they entered the rivers and the caves.
